samples.question: The picture shows five vertical lanes, drawn as five grey vertical lines side by side. At the top of each lane there is one coloured disc: that colour is the colour the lane holds to begin with, and the five starting colours are blue, green, orange, purple and yellow, each used exactly once. Between the lanes there are five black arrows, each drawn horizontally at its own height, each joining two different lanes. An arrow is a one-way copy: the lane at the arrow's tail, the plain end, keeps the colour it is holding, and the lane the arrowhead points at throws away whatever colour it was holding and takes a copy of the colour the tail lane is holding at that moment. Nothing is exchanged: this is a copy and not a swap, so after a copy two lanes hold the same colour and the colour that was overwritten is gone unless some other lane still holds it. The arrows act one at a time, from the topmost arrow down to the bottommost arrow, as the grey arrow in the left margin shows, and a lane's colour keeps changing as later arrows act on it. At the bottom of every lane there is a grey socket, and a red ring marks one of them: the marked lane is the lane whose bottom socket centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring. The colours the lanes hold after the arrows have acted are not drawn anywhere; only the starting discs at the top are drawn. After all five arrows have acted in order from top to bottom, which colour does the marked lane hold? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.
